title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: a Tannakian or 'motivic Galois' setting dated 1965. The neighbouring pages are unrelated SGA1-style descent material (9.4), so this sheet was probably misfiled. The notation can be inferred from the page:
- T is an algebraic torus over Q, the group of a motive M or of a category of motives.
- j: G_m -> T is the weight cocharacter; S = Im j.
- ε: T -> G_m is the Tate or 'cyclotomic' character, with ε∘j(x) = x^α (α = 2 up to sign/normalisation).
- f ∈ T is a Frobenius element with ε(f) = q.
- Hypothesis a) is a positivity or polarisation condition. It says that T_R is 'compact modulo weights': with U the maximal compact subtorus of T_R, we have T_R^0 = U_R·S_R and U ⊂ Ker ε.
- Conclusion c) is the Riemann-hypothesis statement: on every representation E ('vectoriel de déf.') with T acting, the eigenvalues of f have absolute value q^{i/α} on the weight-i part.

Proof that a) implies c):
1. T_R(R) has finitely many components, so some power f^ν (ν > 0) lies in T_R^0. Write f^ν = u·j(x) with u ∈ U(R) and x ∈ R*.
2. U is compact, so the eigenvalues of u on E_C have absolute value 1. Since T is commutative, u and j(x) diagonalise simultaneously.
3. On the weight-i piece the eigenvalues of f^ν therefore have absolute value |x|^i, and those of f have absolute value |x|^{i/ν}.
4. ε is trivial on U, so ε(f)^ν = ε(j(x)) = x^α. Hence |x|^{1/ν} = q^{1/α}, and the eigenvalues of f are Weil q-numbers of weight i (absolute value q^{i/α}).

The abandoned N.B. (struck through in pencil) mentions the case of Q* and something ≃ Z; it is apparently about Frobenius generating a lattice. The last paragraph interprets a) as saying that M carries two superposed structures: a grading structure given by (j, ε) and a 'positive' structure of motivic type. In other words, polarisation is the source of the Weil bounds. This is the Tannakian shadow of Serre's Kähler analogue and of the standard conjecture of Hodge type implying RH.
errors: Minor: x ∈ R* may be negative, so the computation should use |x|. In the same vein, ε|U = 0 (written additively) should read ε trivial on U; this holds automatically for the identity component of a compact torus. Also, ε(f) = q > 0 is needed to take the α-th root. No substantive error otherwise; the argument is correct under hypothesis a).

ideas.what: Frobenius viewed as an element of a torus (the motivic Galois group of a motive over F_q), with weight cocharacter j and Tate character ε
ideas.modern_name: Motivic Galois group / Weil-number torus P(q) or Serre torus; Frobenius element in a Tannakian group
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (idea of motivic Galois groups, mid-1960s, via Serre's accounts); formalised by Saavedra Rivano (1972), Deligne–Milne (1982), Milne (1994, Motives over finite fields)
ideas.where_published: Only indirectly: Récoltes et Semailles mentions motivic Galois groups; the formal treatment is Saavedra, Catégories tannakiennes (LNM 265)

ideas.what: Positivity condition: T_R^0 = U·S with U compact and contained in Ker ε, implies that Frobenius eigenvalues are Weil q-numbers of the expected weights
ideas.modern_name: Polarised Tannakian category / Serre's condition that the weight-quotient is compact (Cartan involution), implying the Riemann hypothesis
ideas.usually_credited_to: Serre (Analogues kählériens, 1960); Grothendieck's standard conjectures (1969); Saavedra (polarisations, 1972); Deligne–Milne; Milne's characterisation of Weil-number tori; Serre's tori S_m (1968)
ideas.where_published: Spirit appears in 'Standard conjectures on algebraic cycles' (1969), where Hodge-type positivity implies the Weil conjectures; the Tannakian/torus form is not in his published texts as far as I know

ideas.what: Interpretation of a) as M carrying superposed grading data (j, ε) and a 'positive' motivic structure
ideas.modern_name: Graded polarised Tannakian category (weight grading plus polarisation)

missed.claim: An explicit 1965 Grothendieck argument, in group-theoretic (torus) language, deducing Weil-number absolute values of Frobenius from compactness of the motivic torus modulo the weight cocharacter. This predates Serre's 1968 tori, Saavedra's polarisations and Milne's Weil-number group. It documents that the 'polarisation implies RH' mechanism was already phrased Tannakian-wise by Grothendieck himself.
missed.quote: Soit U le plus grand sous-tore compact de T_R. Il résulte aisément de l'hyp. a) que T^0_R = U_R·S_R ... et U ⊂ Ker ε
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical priority and attribution for the Tannakian formulation of positivity and Weil numbers (the Serre/Taniyama/Weil-number group circle). The mathematics itself is now standard.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is standard today and a few lines long. However, an explicit 1965 Tannakian/torus proof that positivity gives Weil q-numbers is a notable dated trace of Grothendieck's motivic Galois ideas, which are otherwise known mainly second-hand.
transcription_corrections: In the final paragraph, 'M est limite des deux structures superp.' more likely reads 'M est muni des deux structures superp[osées]'.
'les v.a. des valeurs de f' should read 'v.a. des valeurs propres de f'. The inserted line effectively says the eigenvalues of f have absolute values x^{i/ν}.
'ε|U = 0' is written additively in the original; it means ε is trivial on U.
The crossed-out N.B. block (pencil zigzag) is entirely cancelled and should be marked as deleted.
